test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2021: Official Paper (Held On : 6 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. Holi is the festival of colours which is celebrated not only in India but all cross the world.

B. Then on the next day, people of all ages gather together to play with colours called 'gulal' and coloured water called 'Dulahandi'.

C. People celebrate 'Holika Dahan' on the first day by gathering around and burning piles of wood and cow dung and singing bhajans related to Holi.

D. It is also a festival of unity as it brings people together to celebrate a festivals regardless of caste, ethnicity, or religion.
solution:
The correct answer is "ADCB"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• Let's look at the correct sequence of the passage. 
 
• Statement A is the opening sentence of the passage which explains that the celebration of colours known as Holi is observed worldwide, not just in India.
 
• Statement D is the second sentence of the passage which explains that as it brings people together to enjoy a celebration regardless of caste, nationality, or religion, it is also a festival of togetherness.
 
• Statement C is the third sentence of the passage which explains on the first day, people assemble to celebrate "Holika Dahan," in which they chant bhajans about Holi while burning stacks of cow dung and wood.
 
• Statement B is the last sentence of the passage which shows that then, on the following day, people of all ages congregate to play with "gulal," or coloured paint, and "Dulahandi," or coloured water.

Hence, the correct sequence is A, D, C, B

The correct answer is option 1.

The correct passage is: ***A**. Holi is the festival of colours which is celebrated not only in India but all cross the world. **D**. It is also a festival of unity as it brings people together to celebrate a festivals regardless of caste, ethnicity, or religion. **C**. People celebrate 'Holika Dahan' on the first day by gathering around and burning piles of wood and cow dung and singing bhajans related to Holi. **B**. Then on the next day, people of all ages gather together to play with colours called 'gulal' and coloured water called 'Dulahandi'.*
